# Verifier v1 captured run

`captured-run/` is a format fixture, not proof of live behavior or a complete verifier oracle. It is a fixed byte-for-byte publication produced by the real [`LocalLedgerStore`](../../../src/Parchwell.LoadGen/Run/Ledger/LocalLedgerStore.cs), [`RunEvidenceSession`](../../../src/Parchwell.LoadGen/Run/Evidence/RunEvidenceSession.cs), and [`BlobRunArtifactPublisher`](../../../src/Parchwell.LoadGen/Run/Publication/BlobRunArtifactPublisher.cs) using the deterministic synthetic A01/C0 run in [`GoldenArtifactFixture`](../../Parchwell.LoadGen.Tests/Evidence/GoldenArtifactFixture.cs). The producing test is [`Given_FixedSyntheticRun_When_ProductionWritersCloseArtifacts_Then_BytesMatchCommittedGoldenFiles`](../../Parchwell.LoadGen.Tests/Evidence/GoldenArtifactWriterTests.cs). The fixture uses the A01 baseline resolved through the normal scenario and Kafka configuration path, a two-entry sealed attempt inventory, and fixed run identity and UTC timestamps. It does not load `expected.yaml` or use Kafka/network services; Blob uploads pass through the Azure SDK transport to an in-memory HTTP handler.

The run includes two statistics records in one session. Their timestamp and age pairs preserve one native creation time, and the broker snapshot changes from empty to populated throttle and RTT windows. The raw reports retain the broker's `source` field; the typed snapshots carry the bridge's typed fields. The request lifecycle artifact includes managed native-log and native-error records, with explicit missing source timestamp, correlation ID, and source order on the log record. The ledger has one successful callback row and one synchronous pre-enqueue rejection. Its manifest inventory is independently sealed from the ledger rows. The completion record carries a 12,000,000 microsecond drain boundary; the manifest also retains the standing `broker_lifecycle_inventory_unproven` and `request_lifecycle_capture_unsupported` guards.

The committed test compares every writer output directly with these files. It also reads the index independently, checks each descriptor's byte length and SHA-256 against the payload, then validates the complete artifact set with the production readers. The index lists the five published payloads and has no self-hash. JSON and JSONL writer outputs preserve their actual trailing-newline behavior: `ledger.jsonl`, `manifest.json`, `statistics.jsonl`, and `request-lifecycle.jsonl` end in LF; `capabilities.json` and `index.json` do not.

The captured `applicable_deadline_provenance` claim carries the production catalogue's source list. Its [pinned request code](https://github.com/confluentinc/librdkafka/blob/v2.16.0/src/rdkafka_request.c#L5109-L5127) sets an absolute request timeout from the first message's remaining timeout. The message deadline originates in [pinned message initialization](https://github.com/confluentinc/librdkafka/blob/v2.16.0/src/rdkafka_msg.c#L284-L292), which converts `message_timeout_ms` to microseconds and adds it to the enqueue clock, or uses `INT64_MAX` when that setting is zero. Together these sources support the message-lifetime dependency described by the captured claim; its managed callback attribution remains `unproven`.
